title: Enough for me
hookLine: Allah is enough for me, in Him I trust, Lord of the Throne (9:129)
tomorrow: Block A close: the long surahs

lines: A CAVE, TWO MOSQUES, THREE MEN.
cards: This week, at-Tawbah. It opened with no bismillah, a silence at the door. It took you into a cave with dhat an-nitaqayn, she of the two waistbands.
It called believing men and women protectors of each other. It set two mosques side by side and asked what's under the bricks.
It sat with three men through fifty nights of silence, then painted a messenger who feels your trouble as his own. Now the surah's very last verse.
After the battles, the excuses, the hypocrites and the forgiveness, it ends on a line a person can say at three in the morning.

teach.b: Verse one hundred twenty-nine begins: and if they turn away. It imagines the worst outcome, people rejecting everything the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought. And it tells him what to say.
In Pickthall's translation: "Allah sufficeth me. There is no God save Him. In Him have I put my trust, and He is Lord of the Tremendous Throne."

teach.h: HASBIYA ALLAH — GOD IS MY ENOUGH.
teach.b: In Arabic, it starts hasbiya Allah. Hasb means enough, a sufficiency. Hasbiya: my enough.
God is my enough. Notice what it doesn't say. Not that they won't turn away.
Not that the plan works. It says: even if it doesn't, I'm not empty-handed. Then three steps.
No god but Him, so nothing else gets that place.

teach.h: NO GOD BUT HIM. IN HIM I TRUST.
teach.b: In Him I trust: tawakkul, leaning your whole weight. And the Throne, the Qur'an's picture of God's rule over everything.
The same root runs through another phrase you may hear: hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, God is enough for us, and the best one to rely on.
Bukhari reports that Ibrahim said it when he was thrown into the fire, and the Prophet and his companions said it when they were told an army had gathered against them.
Some Muslims say today's verse seven times, morning and evening, following a report in Abu Dawud that whoever does so, God will be enough for whatever worries him.
A long, hard surah, full of armies and excuses, ends on one person, alone, saying: enough.

how: Some Muslims recite 9:129, hasbiya Allahu la ilaha illa huwa, seven times morning and evening as part of their daily remembrance, and say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil in moments of fear.

games.q: inside the last verse — tap the pairs.
p: said by Ibrahim in the fire

s: 9:129 promises that people won't turn away
it begins 'and if they turn away,' and says God is enough even then.
at-Tawbah's last verse ends on the Throne
in Him I trust, and He is Lord of the Tremendous Throne.
hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil is linked to Ibrahim in Bukhari
Bukhari reports he said it when he was thrown into the fire.

games.q: you've given everything to a message, and people turn away from it. what does the last verse of at-Tawbah tell the Prophet to say?
o: God is enough for me; in Him I trust.
leave them; they're not worth it.
games.why: Allah sufficeth me. no promise the plan works, only that he isn't empty-handed if it doesn't.

practice: Let one real worry come up, the one waiting in the back of your mind, and look at it.

If you pray, you can say the verse's words quietly, hasbiya Allah, God is enough for me, and let the breath out slowly after them; if you don't, notice the weight of the worry and set it down beside you for a while.

wordCard.voice: Hasbiya Allah, God is enough for me. The last verse of at-Tawbah: even if they turn away, He is enough, and in Him I trust. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "God is enough for me," the opening of 9:129, from hasb, a sufficiency.

carryVoice: Your line: allah is enough. Even if the plan fails, you're not empty-handed. A week done, and a surah too.

sources.q: Allah sufficeth me. There is no God save Him. In Him have I put my trust, and He is Lord of the Tremendous Throne.

sources.ref: Qur'an 3:173; Sahih al-Bukhari 4563 (hasbunallah, Ibrahim and the companions)
Sunan Abi Dawud 5081 (saying 9:129 seven times morning and evening)
